claims.text: The phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles initiates when Cu segregates to the surface at high temperature.
Surface-segregated Cu forms a Cu-enriched, liquid-like layer.
The Cu-enriched surface layer locally lowers the melting point and triggers premelting.
Cu-free FeNiCrCo nanoparticles have a higher melting-onset temperature than FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
The comparison uses initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles with a narrow size distribution and Cu-free FeNiCrCo nanoparticle controls.
The proposed heating protocol is an in situ TEM ramp of 5 °C/min to approximately 1200 °C.
EDS mapping and/or XPS will be used to monitor Cu surface segregation.
High-vacuum conditions are intended to prevent oxidation.
Differences among component melting points drive Cu segregation to the nanoparticle surface at elevated temperature.
Cu has a relatively lower melting point than the other relevant alloy components.
The absence of Cu delays development of a liquid-like surface layer.
FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will first exhibit surface-localized liquid-like regions with detectable Cu enrichment.
Melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will progress inward from the surface.
Cu-free nanoparticles will retain structural integrity to higher temperatures than Cu-containing nanoparticles.
Changes in ambient atmosphere or heating rate could alter segregation kinetics and melting progression.
Similar melting onsets in the Cu-containing and Cu-free nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe an earlier liquid-like surface layer in Cu-containing nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to detect significant surface Cu enrichment would falsify the proposed Cu-segregation mechanism.
